Measuring hospital mortality rates can provide some insights, but it may not be sufficient on its own. Our analysis suggests that relying solely on 30-day data may not capture the full picture of hospital mortality.

While cumulative hospital mortality from 180 days postadmission can provide a broader perspective, using only this data may lead to oversimplification and lack of distinction between different time frames.

In contrast, using data on 30 days postadmission might not yield a different perspective than relying solely on 180-day data. This is because the underlying mortality rates and trends may be similar across these time periods.

Therefore, it's essential to consider both 30-day and 180-day mortality data when evaluating hospital performance and making informed decisions. A more comprehensive approach would involve analyzing both datasets to gain a more nuanced understanding of hospital mortality rates.

This recommendation highlights the importance of considering multiple sources of data when assessing hospital performance and developing strategies to improve patient outcomes.
